title: Business Mathematics
intro:
**Simple interest:** I = Prt (r as a decimal, t in years). Amount A = P + I = P(1+rt).

**Compound:** A = P(1 + r/n)^nt if compounded n times a year. Yearly: A=P(1+r)^t.

cards.title: Interest and banking
body: **Simple interest:** I = P × R × T (P = principal, R = rate per year as a decimal, T = time in years). **Compound interest:** interest is added to the principal each period: A = P(
Banks pay interest on savings and charge interest on loans; the loan rate is higher than the savings rate, which is how a bank earns income.

cards.title: Worked example: simple vs compound interest
cards.problem: 10,000 Nfa is saved for 2 years at 6% per year. Compare simple interest with interest compounded yearly.
cards.answer: Compound interest earns 36 Nfa more because year 2 also earns interest on year 1’s interest.

cards.title: Worked: circle angle in the same segment
cards.problem: Points A, B, C, D on a circle. Angle ACB = 35°. Find angle ADB if they stand on the same arc AB.

steps.text: Angles in the same segment (subtended by arc AB) are equal.

cards.title: Partnership: sharing profit
body: Partners usually share profit (or loss) in the **ratio of their capital**. If the money is invested for different lengths of time, use capital × time.

cards.title: Worked example: sharing profit
cards.problem: (a) A invests 30,000 Nfa and B 20,000 Nfa; profit 15,000 Nfa. (b) A invests 20,000 Nfa for 12 months and B 30,000 Nfa for 6 months; profit 14,000 Nfa. Share each profit.
